To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
• Disinformation is a threat to democracy and freedom of expression, but it is not a technological problem.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following question: How should the EU and Member States regulate disinformation with artificial technology in a way that protects freedom of expression and pluralism, and how can they do so in the context of the EU’s legal and political framework?
the use of AI in the fight against disinformation, and its impact on freedom of expression, media pluralism and the democratic functioning of the EU.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the EU should not rush to legislate in the field of disinformation.
the EU has a unique opportunity to lead on the development and deployment of automated content recognition technologies to combat disinformation.
the use of ACR to combat disinformation has a significant potential to enhance freedom of expression and pluralism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the European Union should take the lead in designing and regulating AI disinformation technologies in a manner that is respectful to freedom of expression, and that the use of AI to counter disinformation is a legitimate and effective tool for democracies.
the European Union has the opportunity to take a leadership role in setting the framework to design these technologies in a manner that enhances accountability and respect of free speech.
there is a need to develop a regulatory framework to govern the use of automated content recognition technologies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the EU should take a leadership role in developing the regulatory and technological frameworks to tackle disinformation.
disinformation is not a technological problem but a societal problem.

the European Union has the opportunity to take a leadership role in the regulation of ACR technologies, in particular by developing a framework that is transparent, open and accountable and which is designed with the goal of enhancing free speech and pluralism.
